name: WinPEAP
description: WinPEAP is a WinPE-based workflow to transition devices to Entra Joined and auto-enroll them into Intune via Windows Autopilot. It uses OSDCloud to build a customized WinPE ISO, injects the 4kAutopilotHashUpload.ps1 script and oa3tool-based hardware hash capture, and uploads the Autopilot hash to Intune during WinPE. Automation spans OS deployment, driver injection, hash registration, and enrollment, with support for user-driven Autopilot profiles and VM testing considerations.
author: Beau LaWalt

securityCheck.aiSummary: The WinPEAP code exhibits remote code execution risk due to runtime download and execution of GitHub-hosted scripts, coupled with a setup-time policy bypass that lessens security controls. No hardcoded secrets were detected. Credential flows use standard OAuth mechanisms (client secret or device code) and do not appear to leak credentials, but the dynamic script-loading pathway represents the primary risk. Mitigations include enforcing script integrity (signing, hashing, and pinning), preferring signed local artifacts over remote downloads, and eliminating or properly restricting ExecutionPolicy bypass during deployment.

noRemoteExecution.reason: The WinPEAP bootstrap orchestrator dynamically fetches and executes remote PowerShell scripts from GitHub (Get-RepoScript and the subsequent invocation of the downloaded 4kAutopilotHashUpload.ps1). This creates a significant remote code execution and supply-chain risk: if the GitHub contents are altered or redirected, arbitrary code can run in the WinPE environment. The code includes an offline baked fallback on X:\
